Rebuild rasters from an rij matrix

Source: R/rij.R
rij_matrix_to_raster.Rd

Turns the rows of an rij matrix clipped to an area of interest (AOI) back into rasters on the template's grid, one layer per row, cropped to the AOI raster's extent. An rij matrix is a sparse matrix of feature values: one row per feature (i), one column per template cell with data (j, a planning unit in prioritizr's terms), as made by prioritizr::rij_matrix(). Use it after clip_rij_matrix() to get the AOI's national data as rasters; it builds them in memory and writes nothing.

Usage

rij_matrix_to_raster(rij, template, aoi_raster)

Arguments

rij

The rij matrix clipped to the AOI: a Matrix::dgCMatrix with at least one row, unique row names, and one column per AOI cell with template data, in terra's cell order, as clip_rij_matrix() returns for the same aoi_raster and template.

template

The template raster the rij matrix was built on: a SpatRaster with one layer and a CRS, or a path to a raster file. It sets the output's grid and CRS; only which of its cells have data (are not NA) is used, not its values.

aoi_raster

The AOI as a raster, as given to clip_rij_matrix(): a SpatRaster with one layer, or a path to a raster file, on the template's grid (same CRS, resolution and cell origin). Every cell that is not NA is in the AOI, whatever its value. Its extent sets the output's extent.

Value

A SpatRaster held in memory, with one layer per row of rij, named after the rows, on the template's grid and CRS, cropped to aoi_raster's extent within the template: the row's values in the AOI cells with template data and NA elsewhere.

Method

  • Grid: the template's grid (CRS, resolution and cell origin) cropped to aoi_raster's extent; where aoi_raster reaches past the template's edge, to the part inside the template. No resampling or reprojection.

  • Cells: the AOI cells with template data are worked out from aoi_raster and template as in clip_rij_matrix() (the cells of aoi_raster that are not NA, where the template is not NA, in terra's cell order), and column j of rij fills the j-th of them. The template is read in blocks of rows, so a national template is not held in memory whole.

  • Values: each layer holds its row's values in those cells, 0 where the row stores no value, and NA in every other cell (outside the AOI, or where the template is NA). Values are kept as they are: doubles, not rounded and no areas; rounding for an integer file type is a choice made when writing.

  • Layer names: the row names of rij.

Method choices are recorded in ADR 0013.

See also

rasterize_aoi() to make aoi_raster.

Other rij: clip_rij_matrix(), extract_layers(), read_rij_matrix()

Examples

template <- system.file("extdata", "template.tif", package = "constechr")
aoi <- system.file("extdata", "aoi.gpkg", package = "constechr")
rij <- read_rij_matrix(
  system.file("extdata", "rij.rds", package = "constechr"),
  template
)

# The AOI's cells on the template: a 3 x 3 block, cells 34 to 56
aoi_raster <- rasterize_aoi(aoi, template, cells = "touches")
x <- clip_rij_matrix(rij, aoi_raster, template)
#> Dropped 1 row of `rij` with no values in the AOI: "sp_b".

# One layer per row of x, on the AOI raster's 3 x 3 cells
r <- rij_matrix_to_raster(x, template, aoi_raster)
r
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 3, 3, 2  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 1000, 1000  (x, y)
#> extent      : 1003000, 1006000, 604000, 607000  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#> source(s)   : memory
#> names       : sp_a, cover
#> min values  :    0,     0
#> max values  :    1,   1.6
terra::values(r)
#>       sp_a cover
#>  [1,]    1   0.0
#>  [2,]    1   0.0
#>  [3,]    0   0.0
#>  [4,]    0   0.0
#>  [5,]    1   1.6
#>  [6,]    1   0.0
#>  [7,]    0   0.0
#>  [8,]    0   0.0
#>  [9,]    1   0.0
